Definition: from a compound of G1223 and a derivative of G3717, meaning to straighten thoroughly; rectification, i.e. (specially) the Messianic restauration:--reformation.
BiblicalUsage: Reformation, the setting straight of things, used of the time when the old ordinances of meat and drink and washings give way to the better order Christ brings.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Christ is the reformation the old covenant was waiting for, and nothing in the old order needs patching once He has come.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
